extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, peer reviewers, and scholarly publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and initiatives for improving journal peer review, emphasizing transparency, reviewer training, recognition, and experimental pilots (e.g., registered reports, transparent review). Targeted at stakeholders in scholarly publishing seeking to design or adopt improved peer-review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The theme for Peer Review Week: making the peer-review process more transparent. BMC was an early adopter of open peer review and has produced a report with recommendations on improving peer review for future generations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report recommendations include finding/inventing new ways to identify, verify and invite reviewers; investing in reviewer training; and recognizing reviewers. The page advocates experimenting with initiatives that, if successful, could become standard offerings across Springer Nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports (pre-data peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: A publication format in which the research question and the quality of methodology are peer reviewed before the data are collected and analysed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endorsed as improving transparency and reproducibility; BMC Medicine will offer Registered Reports and has a model tailored for clinical trials. Benefits cited include eliminating hidden outcome switching and publication bias against negative results; quote from Chris Chambers calling it a tremendous step forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review option
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer authors/journals the option to make peer review more transparent (e.g., publishing review reports and related review information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genome Biology and Nature Communications are cited as journals offering options for transparent peer review. Springer Nature may expand such options across titles depending on pilot outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify, verify and invite peer reviewers innovatively
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop new ways of finding, identifying, verifying and inviting peer reviewers to improve reviewer selection and the integrity of review assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation comes from the BMC report; phrased as a key area for investment and invention to improve peer-review quality and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in reviewer training programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide formal training to help researchers learn how to conduct thorough and constructive peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature launched a free online course 'Focus on Peer Review' on the Nature Masterclasses platform, featuring video interviews with editors, experienced reviewers and authors. The course has 4 modules, ~3 hours total including reflection, and offers a course completion certificate. The course claims to go beyond usual 'how-to' training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise and give credit to reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement mechanisms to recognise reviewers for the work they do, ensuring reviewers get the recognition they deserve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition recommendations appear in the BMC report and via initiatives: course completion certificates for training and an example incentive where for every review completed for a particular journal Springer Nature donated a household water filter on behalf of peer reviewers. Over 600 filters have been distributed through this partnership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore and pilot use of Artificial Intelligence in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate the potential role of AI tools to support or enhance aspects of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature is exploring 'grander ideas' such as AI; these are being trialled in small-scale pilots alongside other innovations to assess utility before wider adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial innovations through small-scale pilots before wide adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Use small-scale pilot projects to experiment with new peer-review practices and evaluate success prior to making them standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organisation conducts pilots of innovative practices (e.g., transparent peer review trials, registered-report pilots), and if successful these pilots could be rolled out across journals within Springer Nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review should assess methodological quality rigorously
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers (and formats like Registered Reports) must evaluate the quality of the methodology and research question, not just results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered Reports explicitly tasks peer reviewers with assessing research questions and methods before data collection to improve reproducibility and prevent outcome switching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews should be thorough and constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review ought to be comprehensive and provide constructive feedback to help authors improve manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post notes that researchers report insufficient training in how to conduct thorough and constructive reviews, motivating investment in training and resources (e.g., Masterclasses course) to address this deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide editorial guidance and systems to support review participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should provide guidance, systems and editorial support to editors, reviewers and authors to enable better manuscripts and smoother peer-review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature's in-house editorial staff coordinate the review process, spending substantial time providing guidance and systems to support Editors in Chief, editorial board members, section editors, reviewers and authors. This operational support is framed as fundamental to maintaining scientific quality.
